The coronavirus shock will weigh on near‑term activity and heighten downside risks, but the FOMC’s rapid move to the effective lower bound and large‑scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, alongside expanded repos and dollar swap lines, should mitigate credit‑market frictions and lower external finance premia, consistent with the credit view and balance‑sheet channel evidence (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994; Oliner and Rudebusch, 1996; Gertler and Gilchrist, 1994). With inflation below 2% and expectations little changed, this accommodation aligns with natural‑rate and inflation‑forecast‑targeting frameworks (Friedman–Phelps; Svensson) and VAR evidence that timely easing stabilizes output in downturns (Sims), helping to reduce the risk of a liquidity trap. Overall tone: negative near term, tempered by strong policy support.
